details:
=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:126-137 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, minimax_minimax-m2_5, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, qwen_qwen3_6-plus, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `_post_commit_status_or_error` prints a generic error without the `[integration-pr-readiness]` prefix.
  WHY: The missing stable tag makes readiness-gate failures harder to filter and triage in CI logs.
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:115-120 | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: `_post_commit_status` swallows `SubprocessError`/`OSError` and returns False without printing a warning.
  WHY: CLI/process failures can be hidden, leaving only a generic caller error with no root cause.
- tests/test_check_integration_pr_readiness.py:function `test_main_errors_when_non_orchestrator_status_post_fails` | severity=low | confidence=1
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro]
  PROBLEM: The test only asserts the exit code and does not verify the emitted stderr error.
  WHY: A future regression removing the `::error::` output would still pass this test.
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:59-84 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `_fetch_issue` makes a single `gh issue view` call with no retry for transient failures.
  WHY: A temporary GitHub/API/network blip can make the readiness check fail spuriously instead of recovering on a retry.
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:~142-161 | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [moonshotai_kimi-k2_5, x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `--head-ref` and `--head-sha` are consumed without format validation.
  WHY: Malformed values can reach `gh api` or produce ambiguous error statuses.
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:_post_commit_status_or_error (lines ~126-137) and non-orchestrator path | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The new wrapper fails closed on POST error even when the non-orchestrator path would otherwise be a no-op success.
  WHY: A flaky status API now turns unrelated PRs into hard failures instead of the documented neutral exit-0 path.
- scripts/lint_plan_archival_completeness.py:_fetch_issue_via_gh (lines ~88-102) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: `gh issue view` failures are collapsed to `None` without retry.
  WHY: Transient GitHub API flakes can spuriously block the lint.
- scripts/lint_plan_archival_completeness.py:label parsing one-liner (line 104 in workflow) | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The label extraction one-liner consumes unsanitized JSON in `python3 -c`.
  WHY: A crafted label can turn into arbitrary command execution in the `pull_request` workflow context.
- scripts/lint_plan_archival_completeness.py:_has_descope_section_content (lines ~148-162) | severity=medium | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The heading-level check rejects valid nested de-scope sections.
  WHY: A `##` heading followed by `###` subsections can still be rejected before the bullet list is seen, blocking legitimate archival PRs.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:external-finalize gate (~8572-8627) and state write for `external_finalize_partial_alert_sig` | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: The dedup signature write is not locked or atomic.
  WHY: Concurrent poll runs can race and leave stale or truncated state, causing repeated WARNING alerts.
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py:`issue_label_cache` handling of `None` (lines ~158-183) | severity=medium | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [x-ai_grok-4_20]
  PROBLEM: A transient label lookup failure caches `None` as if no tracking label exists.
  WHY: Later checks in the same PR can silently skip real violations after one early API error.
- tests/test_check_integration_pr_readiness.py:function `test_main_errors_when_non_orchestrator_status_post_fails` and `test_main_errors_when_failure_status_cannot_be_posted` | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [qwen_qwen3_6-plus]
  PROBLEM: The new tests do not assert the posted state and description parameters.
  WHY: A future regression could post the wrong metadata and still pass because the tests only check that `_post_commit_status` returns False.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:lines 126-137, function `_post_commit_status_or_error` | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The error message emitted when a commit-status POST fails lacks the structured `[integration-pr-readiness]` prefix that every other error/warning path in `main()` uses.
  WHY: Downstream log-analysis tooling that greps for `[integration-pr-readiness]` to detect readiness-gate failures will miss POST-failure errors entirely.
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:lines 115-120, function `_post_commit_status` | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: When `subprocess.run` raises `subprocess.SubprocessError` or `OSError`, the function returns `False` without printing any warning to stderr.
  WHY: The caller only emits a generic failure message, so the underlying `gh`/process problem is silently swallowed.
- tests/test_check_integration_pr_readiness.py:function `test_main_errors_when_non_orchestrator_status_post_fails` (added by last run diff) | confidence=1
  PROBLEM: The test does not verify that `_post_commit_status_or_error` prints the `::error::` message to stderr.
  WHY: It only checks `rc == 1`, so a regression that removes the error output would still pass.
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:function `_fetch_issue`, lines 69-84 | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `_fetch_issue` makes a single `gh issue view` call with no retry on transient failures.
  WHY: A temporary GitHub API/network blip can make the readiness check fail spuriously instead of recovering on a retry.
=== END FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===

  PROBLEM: The error message emitted when POST fails lacks the structured `[integration-pr-readiness]` prefix used in other error messages in the same script.
  WHY: Without the consistent prefix, log analysis tooling and operators cannot easily filter and classify readiness-gate failures versus other workflow errors.

=== FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py:_post_commit_status_or_error() function (the new helper introduced in LAST RUN DIFF, lines ~126-137) | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: The generic ::error:: message lacks the [integration-pr-readiness] structured prefix used by every other error path in this script.
  WHY: Operators and log-analysis tooling that grep for the stable [integration-pr-readiness] prefix will not correlate this failure with the readiness gate.
- tests/test_check_integration_pr_readiness.py:test_main_errors_when_non_orchestrator_status_post_fails (new test in LAST RUN DIFF) and test_main_errors_when_failure_status_cannot_be_posted (new test) | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Both new test mocks `_post_commit_status` to return False but do not capture or assert on the posted state and description parameters.
  WHY: A future regression could post the wrong metadata before failing, and these tests would still pass because they only check the return value.
=== END FINDINGS FROM qwen_qwen3_6-plus ===

=== FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
- scripts/lint_plan_archival_completeness.py `_fetch_issue_via_gh` (lines ~88-102) and label parsing one-liner (line 104 in workflow) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `gh issue view` failures are collapsed to `None` with no retry, and label extraction uses a `python3 -c` one-liner on unsanitized JSON.
  WHY: Transient GitHub API flakes or a crafted label containing shell metacharacters can cause the lint to either block spuriously or execute arbitrary commands in the `pull_request` workflow context.
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py argument parsing and `_fetch_issue` (lines ~142-161, 59-68) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: `--head-ref` and `--head-sha` are consumed without format validation; all `gh` failures become `None`.
  WHY: Malformed or malicious branch/SHA values reach `gh api` or cause ambiguous error statuses; transient API errors are treated as a missing tracking issue.
- scripts/lint_plan_archival_completeness.py `_has_descope_section_content` (lines ~148-162) | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The heading-level check (`<= descope_level`) stops at any same-or-higher heading, but the comment and test claim it allows sub-headings before list items.
  WHY: A valid archival PR with `## De-scoped phases` followed by `### Phase 2` then a bullet list is incorrectly rejected, blocking legitimate merges.
- scripts/check_integration_pr_readiness.py `_post_commit_status_or_error` (lines ~126-137) and non-orchestrator path | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The new wrapper now fails closed on POST error even for non-orchestrator branches.
  WHY: When the GitHub status API is flaky, unrelated PRs lose the required status context and are blocked even though the readiness check “does not apply”.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh external-finalize gate (~8572-8627) and state write for `external_finalize_partial_alert_sig` | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The dedup signature write uses no lock, atomic replace, or retry; multiple poll runs can race.
  WHY: Concurrent cron invocations can truncate the state file or leave an old signature, causing repeated WARNING alerts and operator fatigue.
- scripts/lint_pr_body_auto_close.py `issue_label_cache` handling of `None` (lines ~158-183) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: Transient lookup failure stores `None` in the cache; subsequent matches reuse it as “no tracking label”.
  WHY: A single early API error can silently suppress later violations for the same issue in the same PR, weakening the required check.
=== END FINDINGS FROM x-ai_grok-4_20 ===
